html:
Manchuria is the region of northeast China north of Korea, a land of forests, rivers and the fertile plains of the Liao and Songhua rivers. The map shows it as its own territory in 1920, 1930 and 1945, when it was largely outside the control of China's government.

It is the homeland of the Tungusic peoples, including the Manchus, who conquered China in 1644 as the Qing. For a long time the Qing kept Chinese settlers out. In the late 1800s Russia built railways across it, and Chinese farmers poured in. Japan won the southern railway and Port Arthur from Russia in the Russo-Japanese War of 1904 and 1905.

In the map's years:

  • 1920: the warlord Zhang Zuolin ruled it as his own domain. Japanese officers killed him with a bomb in 1928.
  • 1930: his son Zhang Xueliang held it, loyal in name to the Nationalist government.
  • 1931: Japan's army staged the Mukden Incident and seized the region. In 1932 it set up Manchukuo, with Puyi, the last Qing emperor, as figurehead.
  • 1945: the Soviet Union invaded in August and destroyed Japan's army there within weeks.

After the war Manchuria went back to China and became the communists' main base in the civil war that followed.
